recap_pending.story: Gary is at home on a Monday afternoon, focused on securing his golf cart wiring with spare fuses and zip ties from his toolbox. Over on Magnolia Loop, Donna is determined to make Rosa's six o'clock supper, insisting she'll arrive with bells on and asking Rosa to pass along word to Gary about their doubles ladder match. Hal, dutifully keeping the committee's books, is tallying the pink flamingos visible from the street, while Rosa hopefully invites him to pot roast and tells him the count can wait.
dialogue: Donna said to Rosa: “Rosa, six tonight is perfect, no need to build around me, I'll be there with bells on. And if you spot Gary before I do, tell him his doubles partner is hunting for him, we have a ladder match to win!”
Rosa said to Hal: “Hal, Donna's coming at six tonight and I'm setting a place for you too. No pressure about the flamingo count, it'll still be here after pot roast. Can I count on you?”

recap_pending.story: At 1:17 on a mild Monday afternoon in Sumter Oaks, Gary is at home focused on zip-tying the wiring runs and fitting spare fuses into his golf cart's amp and light circuits. Donna and Rosa are both determined and heading toward the Rec Center, while Hal, gruffly warm as ever, promises Rosa he'll show up at six sharp with something in hand so he isn't empty-handed. The flamingos on Magnolia Loop will have to wait until after dinner.
dialogue: Hal said to Rosa: “You can count on me, Rosa. Six sharp, and I'll bring something so I'm not showing up empty-handed. The flamingos can keep till after dinner.”
